llm.summary: The skill is a coherent GitHub MCP integration, but it asks for broad GitHub API authority with broad activation triggers and little built-in scoping or confirmation guidance.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to browse repositories, search code, manage issues and PRs, monitor CI/CD, fork repositories, create branches, and automate GitHub operations; that is coherent but includes high-impact read/write GitHub authority.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The activation language includes generic terms such as github, code, and search and also covers any GitHub-related operation requiring API access, which is too broad for a skill that can perform account- or repository-changing actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The setup is disclosed as mcporter configuration for either a remote HTTP MCP endpoint or a local github-mcp-server binary; no hidden install hooks were evident, but the remote token-bearing configuration deserves review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: A GitHub token is proportionate for GitHub API access, but the artifact does not clearly require least-privilege scopes, repository limits, or explicit confirmation before write operations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not show background workers or privilege escalation, but the MCP configuration and any GitHub changes it performs can persist beyond the session.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to use a GitHub MCP server with your GitHub token. Use the narrowest token scopes and repository access possible, prefer explicit confirmation before creating branches, opening or modifying PRs/issues, or touching CI/CD resources, and be aware the broad triggers may activate the skill during ordinary GitHub, code, or search requests.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger concern is supported by the artifact and matters more here because the skill can use GitHub credentials for mutating operations; this supports Review, not a malicious verdict.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean, so it does not add a negative signal and is not the basis for the Review verdict.
